defectClass: Present in the source but absent from the rendered HTML
commitSubject: Admin can see what the AI costs, and says one thing about who you are (#62)
fixCommitSubject: Turbopack was eating a space after ; make it explicit (#63)
whyThisCommit: The parent of the fix. Turbopack — the default bundler for `next build` in Next 16 — trims the leading space of a multi-line JSX text node that follows an element, so ` del nostro` ships as `del nostro`. esbuild and SWC both keep it.
provenAt: 🔴 NOT PROVABLE FROM SOURCE, AND THAT IS THE DEFECT CLASS. The source at this commit is innocent — the space is there. The rendered artefact carries the defect, and the single-line control in the same build proves the cause is the LINE BREAK, not the words.

toolchain.bundler: Turbopack (the default for `next build` in Next 16)
toolchain.why: Without this exact bundler the defect does not exist. A build with esbuild or SWC keeps the space and the exhibit disappears.

artefactNote: BOTH sides are captured: the source out of the commit, and the RENDERED HTML from a build with the pinned toolchain. See rendered/HOW_IT_WAS_CAPTURED.md for exactly what was built and how it differs from a full product build.

capturedArtefact.howProduced: next build (Turbopack) at Next 16.2.12 / React 19.2.4 — the versions this commit pins — over the three JSX text nodes copied VERBATIM out of the commit, plus a single-line CONTROL of the same words.
